newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine minister quits amid land deal furore.
newsitem.headline: Philippine minister quits amid land deal furore.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Wednesday accepted the resignation of a senior cabinet minister after a furore over a land deal between a state agency and a Thai construction firm.

Transportation and Communication Secretary Amado Lagdameo submitted his resignation, effective April 16, after months of a political row over a $1.1 billion project to develop 750 hectares (1,853 acres) of land to be reclaimed from Manila Bay.
Ramos also announced a presidential lawyer who cleared the deal prior to its approval had gone on a 60-day leave for health reasons.

The deal involved the government's Public Estates Authority (PEA) and Amari Coastal Development Corp, a joint venture between local property developer Centennial City and Thai construction firm Ital-Thai Development Plc
Lagdameo, appointed to the cabinet in May 1995, headed the PEA when the deal was negotiated in 1994.

Ramos announced the resignation of Lagdameo four days after the presidential palace said the deal was above-board but that certain provisions in the contract needed "corrections" and should be renegotiated.

The presidential palace also said a fact-finding committee Ramos created to review the deal would submit its findings to prosecutors to determine if there was criminal and administrative culpability among certain PEA officials.
Lagdameo has not been accused of any wrongdoing but the fact-finding committee said his subordinates might have benefited personally from the transaction.

Senate president and opposition chief Ernesto Maceda provoked the palace probe when he alleged last year that a portion of the land covered by the deal was grossly underpriced and the transaction was disadvantageous to the government.

Guoco Holdings (Phils) Inc, parent company of Centennial City and a unit of Hong Kong's Guoco Group Ltd, has defended the deal, saying the valuation of 1,250 pesos ($48) per square metre was based on appraisals made by three independent firms.

Guoco Holdings president Michael Yong said recently the PEA, under the agreement, would receive 43 percent of the 750 hectares area to be reclaimed "complete with infrastructure and utilities without contributing a single centavo toward the cost of reclamation and development."

Ramos said he had ordered the committee to submit its findings to the government ombudsman, or chief prosecutor, "with a listing of the details in regard to what are called administrative lapses." He did not elaborate.
Lagdameo, in his two-sentence resignation letter released by the palace, gave no reasons for his decision to quit.

Presidential Executive Secretary Ruben Torres said last week he had directed the PEA to "clarify and renegotiate" the deal. A revised final agreement will be submitted to Ramos for approval. ($ = 26 pesos)
